applies_why: The judge text does not count any cited verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link; it labels the issue UNDERDETERMINED and says it was answered.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: 'counts as an unanswered witness' and 'counts toward a broken link': one reading is that merely mentioning or treating cited verses as real counts them toward a broken link; the other is that the judge must actually count a verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link, which this text does not do.
why: The judge says the issue is UNDERDETERMINED and answered in the named rounds, so it does not count any verse as an unanswered witness toward a broken link.
